source.work: Firebase Firestore documentation, order and limit data
source.paraphrase: Bound every read with limit() or a where() filter so one call cannot download the whole collection.

invariants.why: An unbounded getDocs scales cost and latency with the collection, not the screen. One careless call on a large collection bills thousands of reads.
invariants.fixHint: Wrap the source in query() with limit(n) or where(field, op, value). Pick the page size the caller chose.
invariants.avoid: query(col) with no constraint still reads everything. A limit applied in a different statement does not bound this call.

source.work: Firebase Firestore documentation, set a document
source.paraphrase: setDoc without merge intentionally creates or replaces a document. Pass merge only when the write is partial.

invariants.why: A partial overwrite can remove fields, but replacing an entire document is also a documented operation. The syntax cannot distinguish intent.
invariants.fixHint: Pass { merge: true } as the third argument, or use updateDoc for a partial write to an existing document.
invariants.avoid: An empty options object carries no merge flag. A data field named merge does not count as the option.

source.work: Firebase Firestore documentation, document and collection references
source.paraphrase: Build references from separate path segments. Concatenated strings defeat Security Rules path matching.

invariants.why: A concatenated path is opaque text at review time. Rules match on segments, so a joined string can slip past the rule the author intended.
invariants.fixHint: Pass each segment as its own argument: doc(db, "orders", id) instead of doc(db, "orders/" + id).
invariants.avoid: Template literals are the same concatenation in backticks. Joining segments in a helper still hides the shape.

source.paraphrase: A write batch does nothing until commit() runs. Never leave a batch uncommitted.

invariants.why: A batch needs a commit before its lifecycle ends. A per-statement pattern cannot prove whether a later statement commits it.
invariants.fixHint: Chain commit onto the writeBatch statement so the batch cannot be created without being sent.
invariants.avoid: commit in a later statement is invisible to this rule and to hurried readers. Awaiting the batch object itself commits nothing.

source.work: Cloud Firestore documentation, Transactions and batched writes (firebase.google.com)
source.paraphrase: In a Firestore transaction, all read operations must come before any write operations; calling transaction.get() after set, update, or delete fails at runtime.

invariants.why: Firestore rejects any transaction.get() executed after a transaction write with 'Firestore transactions require all reads to be executed before all writes'.
invariants.fixHint: Move all transaction.get() calls to the top of the runTransaction callback before any transaction.set, transaction.update, or transaction.delete calls.
invariants.avoid: Matches transaction callbacks where the parameter is named tx, transaction, or t and a get() statement follows a set/update/delete statement in the same block.
